findings.description: The RTL current appointment visually reads 16:00–14:00 although the supplied display-ready time is 14:00–16:00. Other context is aligned for RTL, but the numeric range has changed visual order.
findings.rootCause: VisitText uses TextDirection.Content for every string. A numeric-only time range has no strong direction and inherits RTL paragraph direction.

evidence.details: The text node retains semantic label 14:00–16:00 while the screenshot displays the endpoint groups reversed.

findings.description: Native child identifiers are overwritten by visit.panel. Titles, context, rows, consent and terminal buttons all report visit.panel instead of their required distinct IDs. Every supplied actionable iOS script consequently reports its intended target unobserved and does not execute the activation.
findings.rootCause: The outer VStack assigns accessibilityIdentifier visit.panel without an explicit accessibility containment element, propagating that identifier to native descendants.

findings.description: Rows expose a generic native Other element (role_raw 1) rather than a native button/control element. The unavailable s10 and w11 rows report enabled=true instead of native disabled state, despite being visually dimmed. Selected flags and coherent row labels do survive.
findings.rootCause: The row applies accessibilityElement(children: .ignore) after the Button and disabled modifier, then adds only selected traits. This replaces the native control exposure without restoring the button and not-enabled traits.

findings.description: PlainButtonStyle applies an additional disabled fade to the fully styled labels/backgrounds. Unavailable row time, detail, status and reason are faded, and disabled confirmation buttons also have substantially weaker colors/contrast than specified.
findings.rootCause: The row and primary Button styles combine custom explicit palette colors with PlainButtonStyle and disabled, allowing native disabled opacity to alter the intended full-opacity treatment.
